message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"b7e2f8441bc051e6358079d35649f8fa00ccbba1fdb8660bca3439dbfee2e796","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wa-class-std:lineage:81","source_registry_sha256":"9f6e1cb1188348b60e3a496c6f0991207e113d4c5c50fdea6643147e46e0832e","units":[{"unit_id":"sec01-u01","module_id":"sec01-m01","objective_ids":["sec01-u01"],"title":{"text":"Your WDL number and residency","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Every Washington license, permit and ID card carries a personal number that often starts with WDL, and License Express accounts must be in your own name.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]},{"text":"A licensed adult newcomer has thirty days to get a Washington license, while a newcomer under eighteen enters the intermediate license system.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F06","sec01-R11"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Sam, aged twenty-six, has just moved to Washington with a valid license from Oregon.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A new resident aged eighteen or older who is licensed in another state has thirty days to get a Washington license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04"]},"result":{"text":"Sam has thirty days to get a Washington driver license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking an out-of-state license stays good in Washington indefinitely.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04"]},"correction":{"text":"A licensed adult newcomer has thirty days to get a Washington driver license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R11"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Adults switch in thirty days; teens enter the intermediate system.","fact_ids":["sec01-R11"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A nineteen-year-old newcomer holds a valid license from Idaho. How long do they have to get a Washington license?","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R11"]},"answer":{"text":"Thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04"]},"rationale":{"text":"A licensed newcomer aged eighteen or older has thirty days to get a Washington driver license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R11"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Starting your Washington license","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Your personal WDL number.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F04"]},{"text":"Who counts as a resident.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F04"]},{"text":"Deadlines for newcomers.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the first lesson on getting your Washington license. Before any exam or permit, the guide sets out a few basics. Every Washington license, permit and ID card carries a personal Washington number that often starts with the letters WDL. You also need to know when you count as a resident, and what a newcomer must do after moving here with a license from another state. This lesson covers those rules, the new-resident deadlines, and what the guide says about REAL ID. Let us take them one at a time so each rule is clear.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"WDL number and License Express","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Every card carries a personal WDL number.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]},{"text":"License Express is the secure DOL website.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]},{"text":"Open an account in your own name.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Start with your number. Every Washington license, permit and ID card carries a personal Washington number, and it often starts with the letters WDL. Next is License Express, the secure DOL website for licensing services. Each new driver must open a License Express account in their own name, because services cannot be obtained through someone else's account. So a teen cannot simply use a parent's account to handle their own license. The number and the account both belong to you personally, and the guide treats them that way from the very first step.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Who counts as a resident","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Any single listed condition is enough.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]},{"text":"Examples: a home here, voter registration.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]},{"text":"Also: Washington tax address, state assistance.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Residency matters because it decides when Washington rules apply to you. You count as a Washington resident when any single listed condition applies. The guide's examples include keeping a home here for personal use, being registered to vote here, filing taxes with a Washington address, or receiving state public assistance. Notice the word single. You do not need all of the conditions, or even two of them. One listed condition is enough to make you a resident, and once you are a resident the new-resident deadlines that come next start to matter for you.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Licensed adult newcomers","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Eighteen or older, licensed elsewhere: thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},{"text":"Expired license: pass both exams.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Now the deadline for newcomers. A new resident aged eighteen or older who is licensed in another state has thirty days to get a Washington driver license. That is a firm window, not an open-ended grace period. There is one important twist. If the new resident's out-of-state license has already expired, they must pass both the knowledge exam and the skills exam before Washington will license them. So a valid license from another state gives you the thirty-day switch, but an expired one sends you through both exams. To remember: eighteen or older, licensed elsewhere: thirty days; expired license: pass both exams.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Newcomers under eighteen","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Apply for an Intermediate Driver License.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R11"]},{"text":"DOL approves the driver education.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R11"]},{"text":"At least six months of permit time.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Newcomers under eighteen follow a different path. A new resident under eighteen who holds another state's license applies for a Washington Intermediate Driver License. DOL must approve their driver education and confirm at least six months of instruction-permit time. In other words, a teen newcomer does not simply swap cards the way an adult does. They enter the same intermediate system that Washington teens use, with its own passenger, night-hour and phone limits, which you will meet in a later lesson of this section.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Adult or teen newcomer?","fact_ids":["sec01-R11","sec01-F04","sec01-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: every newcomer gets thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec01-R11","sec01-F04","sec01-F06"]},{"text":"Adults switch within thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec01-R11","sec01-F04","sec01-F06"]},{"text":"Under eighteen enters the intermediate system.","fact_ids":["sec01-R11","sec01-F04","sec01-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Because the thirty-day rule is easy to remember, many learners apply it to every newcomer. The guide limits it to a licensed adult newcomer, someone aged eighteen or older with a license from another state. A newcomer under eighteen must enter the intermediate license system instead, with DOL approving their driver education and confirming their permit time. When a question gives you a newcomer, check the age first. Eighteen or older with a valid license points to thirty days. Under eighteen points to the intermediate license.","fact_ids":["sec01-R11","sec01-F04","sec01-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check: the newcomer deadline","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R11","sec01-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"A nineteen-year-old arrives licensed from Idaho.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R11","sec01-F05"]},{"text":"How long to get a Washington license?","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R11","sec01-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a nineteen-year-old has just moved to Washington and holds a valid license from Idaho. How long do they have to get a Washington driver license? Think it through before the answer. They are eighteen or older and licensed in another state, so the adult newcomer rule applies. The answer is thirty days. If their Idaho license had expired, they would instead need to pass both the knowledge exam and the skills exam. And if they were under eighteen, they would apply for an intermediate license instead.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R11","sec01-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Residency and REAL ID recap","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"WDL number and own account.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F07"]},{"text":"One condition makes you a resident.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F07"]},{"text":"REAL ID is a law, not a card.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, your WDL number is personal, and your License Express account must be in your own name. One listed condition is enough to make you a resident. A licensed adult newcomer has thirty days, an expired license means both exams, and a newcomer under eighteen enters the intermediate system. Finally, REAL ID is a law rather than a card. An enhanced license or ID is one of several options that satisfy it, and a standard license will no longer be accepted at airport security, border crossings or secure federal buildings.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F06","sec01-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u02","module_id":"sec01-m02","objective_ids":["sec01-u02"],"title":{"text":"The instruction permit","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]},"why_how":[{"text":"You need a WDL number before applying for a permit, and the permit age depends on whether you enroll in driver training.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]},{"text":"The permit lasts one year while a passing knowledge score lasts two years.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R02"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ava is fifteen and has just enrolled in a driver training course that starts next week.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09"]},"reasoning":{"text":"With driver training you may apply for a permit as young as fifteen, from one to ten days before the course starts.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09"]},"result":{"text":"Ava may apply for her permit now, online or at an office.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the permit age is fifteen and a half for everyone.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"Fifteen and a half applies only without a course; with driver training the permit age is fifteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Course at fifteen, no course at fifteen and a half.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A permit holder passed the knowledge exam. Which lasts longer, the permit or the passing score?","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R02"]},"answer":{"text":"The passing score, which lasts two years.","fact_ids":["sec01-R02"]},"rationale":{"text":"The permit is valid for one year, while a passing knowledge exam score stays valid for two years.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Getting your instruction permit","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"WDL number first.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"Two permit ages.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"Two validity periods.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers the instruction permit, the first step for a new Washington driver. There are three things to master. First, the prerequisite: you must already have a WDL number before you apply. Second, the two permit ages, which depend on whether you enroll in a driver training course. Third, the two validity periods, one for the permit itself and one for a passing knowledge exam score. Each pair of numbers is easy to swap, so we will set them side by side and keep them straight. To remember: wDL number first; two permit ages; two validity periods.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The driver training path","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"WDL number before applying.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Permit as young as fifteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},{"text":"Apply one to ten days before class.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Begin with the prerequisite. You must already have a WDL number before you apply for an instruction permit. Then look at the driver training path. When you enroll in driver training, you may apply for a permit as young as fifteen. You can apply online or at an office, and the timing is set: from one to ten days before the course starts. So the permit is lined up with the start of the course. This is the earlier of the two permit paths, and it is tied to being enrolled in a training course. To remember: wDL number before applying; permit as young as fifteen; apply one to ten days before class.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The path without training","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Knowledge exam after fifteen and a half.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-R01"]},{"text":"Permit once you pass.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-R01"]},{"text":"Skills exam and license wait until eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"The second path skips driver training. Without a course, you may take the knowledge exam after turning fifteen and a half, and you get the permit once you pass. The cost of this path comes later. The skills exam and the license must wait until you are eighteen. So the no-course path starts half a year later, and it also pushes the license itself out to age eighteen. When a question describes a teen with no training course, these are the numbers to reach for. To remember: knowledge exam after fifteen and a half; permit once you pass; skills exam and license wait until eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Two ages, two validity periods","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: one permit age for all.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"Course fifteen, no course fifteen and a half.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"Permit one year, score two years.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap, and it has two parts. First, the permit ages. The permit age with a driver training course is fifteen, while the age through the knowledge exam without a course is fifteen and a half, so the course path starts half a year sooner. Second, the validity periods. An instruction permit is valid for one year and can be renewed for a fee, while a passing knowledge exam score stays valid for two years. Keep each number with its own subject so the pairs never swap places. To remember: course fifteen, no course fifteen and a half; permit one year, score two years.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check: what lasts longer?","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Permit or passing knowledge score?","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"Which one outlasts the other?","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a permit holder passed the knowledge exam. Which lasts longer, the instruction permit or the passing knowledge exam score? Work it out before the answer. The permit is valid for one year and can be renewed for a fee. The passing score stays valid for two years. So the answer is the passing score, which lasts two years. The guide's warning follows from this: wait too long before the skills exam and you may have to retake the knowledge exam. A helpful hook for this lesson: course at fifteen, no course at fifteen and a half.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Permit recap","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-R01","sec01-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"WDL number first.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-R01","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"Fifteen with a course, fifteen and a half without.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-R01","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"Permit one year, score two.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-R01","sec01-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, get your WDL number before you apply for the permit. With driver training you may apply as young as fifteen, from one to ten days before the course starts. Without training you may take the knowledge exam after fifteen and a half and get the permit when you pass, but the skills exam and license wait until eighteen. The permit lasts one year and can be renewed for a fee, and a passing knowledge exam score lasts two years. Those numbers set up everything in the next lesson. To remember: wDL number first; fifteen with a course, fifteen and a half without; permit one year, score two.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-R01","sec01-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u03","module_id":"sec01-m03","objective_ids":["sec01-u03"],"title":{"text":"A teen's first license","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F14"]},"why_how":[{"text":"A teen license at sixteen or seventeen needs six months on the permit, residency, an approved course, logged practice and a clean record.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F14","sec01-F15"]},{"text":"The forty daytime and ten nighttime hours make the fifty hours the parent certifies.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F16"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Leo is sixteen, has held his permit for seven months, finished an approved course and logged forty day and ten night hours with his aunt, who has four years of experience.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F14"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A teen needs six months on the permit, age sixteen, residency, an approved course, and forty day plus ten night hours beside a driver with three or more years of experience.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F14","sec01-R03"]},"result":{"text":"Leo meets the permit-time, course and practice-hour requirements, as long as his record is also clean.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F14","sec01-F15"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the parent certifies fifty hours on top of the forty day and ten night hours.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"The forty daytime plus ten nighttime hours are the same fifty hours the parent or guardian certifies.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F16"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Forty plus ten makes the fifty.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A teen logged forty daytime hours and ten nighttime hours. What total does the parent certify on the form?","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F16"]},"answer":{"text":"Fifty hours.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05"]},"rationale":{"text":"The forty daytime and ten nighttime hours add up to the fifty hours the parent or guardian certifies.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F16"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Earning a teen license","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F14","sec01-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Permit time and a course.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F14","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"Practice hours and a clean record.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F14","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"How the license is issued.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F14","sec01-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers how a teen earns a first license at sixteen or seventeen. The guide lists several requirements that must all be met: time on the permit, minimum age, residency, an approved traffic safety course, logged practice hours with a qualified supervisor, a clean driving record, and a parent or guardian's signed form. After that comes the issuing process, with exam scores recorded by the school and a temporary license until the card arrives. We will take the requirements first and the issuing steps last. To remember: permit time and a course; practice hours and a clean record; how the license is issued.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F14","sec01-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Permit time and the course","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Six months on the permit, age sixteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]},{"text":"Live in Washington.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]},{"text":"Approved traffic safety course.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"To get a first license at sixteen or seventeen, you must have held the permit for at least six months, be at least sixteen, live in Washington, and complete a traffic safety course at an approved driver training school. A course finished in another state can count, but only if it meets Washington's minimum of thirty classroom hours and six behind-the-wheel hours. So an out-of-state course is not automatically accepted. It has to reach those two Washington minimums before it counts toward your license. To remember: six months on the permit, age sixteen; live in Washington; approved traffic safety course.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Practice hours and supervisor","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-R03","sec01-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Forty daytime and ten nighttime hours.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-R03","sec01-R05"]},{"text":"Supervisor with three or more years.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-R03","sec01-R05"]},{"text":"Attested by a parent or guardian.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-R03","sec01-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Next are the practice hours. A teen applicant must log at least forty hours of daytime driving and ten hours of nighttime driving. That practice happens beside a licensed driver with three or more years of experience, and a parent, guardian or responsible adult attests to it. The supervisor's experience is worth remembering exactly, because the adult permit route uses a different number. For teens, the supervising driver needs three or more years. Together, the day and night hours add up to fifty. To remember: forty daytime and ten nighttime hours; supervisor with three or more years; attested by a parent or guardian.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-R03","sec01-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Clean record and parent form","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Six months with no violations.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"No alcohol or drug offenses on the permit.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"Parent certifies fifty hours.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"The record requirement comes next. A teen applicant must go six months with no traffic violations or convictions before applying, and must have no alcohol or drug offenses while driving on the permit. For an in-person teen application, a parent or guardian signs an authorization form. On that form they certify at least fifty hours of driving experience and no traffic infractions or violations during the previous six months. So the form ties together the practice hours and the clean record. To remember: six months with no violations; no alcohol or drug offenses on the permit; parent certifies fifty hours.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The fifty-hour total","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-R03","sec01-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: fifty hours on top of forty plus ten.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-R03","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"Forty day plus ten night is fifty.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-R03","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"Teen supervisor needs three years.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-R03","sec01-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap.
